title: Cortex RefinePunchupRequest (DRAFT v0)
description: What a surface (PLO/pocket-agent/fleet-terminal) sends to the refine-punchup gate. Per ADR-0014, authored once in cortex/contracts/ and imported by every consumer. Surfaces-Builder is the named consumer; agent-fabric's in-process engine is the named producer (ADR-0023 retired the n8n spine). Status: DRAFT v0. v0→v1 promotion gated on a real end-to-end round-trip through the engine.

id.description: Client-generated idempotency key. Stable across retries. Server SHOULD return the cached prior response if id was seen within the last 5 minutes; otherwise re-refine. The engine does NOT cache today; client-side dedupe is the only safety until the v0 contract's server-side cache lands.

envelope.description: The raw TaskEnvelope. At intake, refined_prompt is null; the spine writes the punched-up spec back. The envelope's id MUST equal the top-level id (consistency check on the server side). Permissive on additional properties (additionalProperties: true): real envelopes from surfaces' normalizeSurfaceIntent have ~26 fields (metadata, created_at, updated_at, attempts, result, error, etc.) beyond the canonical TaskEnvelope. The inlined subset here is the minimum the gate needs to do its work; the server MUST accept envelopes with additional fields and pass them through. v1 design question: should the canonical TaskEnvelope schema also be loosened to admit adapter-specific fields like metadata? Separate ADR conversation.

surface.description: Originating surface. Lifts the WorkRequestSource enum verbatim; NOT redefined. Used to route clarifications back and to scope the Mnemos container.

request_id.description: Optional caller-supplied tracing key, distinct from the idempotency key. Used for logging/observability only; the spine does NOT use this for dedup. If unset, the spine generates one.
